title: Cloud Quota and Service Limit Utilization

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:service_quotas` events with `matching activity` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.4.17 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:service_quotas` traffic without `matching activity`. Confirm UC-4.4.17 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:service_quotas` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`, Service Quotas API, Azure quotas, GCP quotas; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: `Splunk_TA_aws`, Service Quotas API, Azure quotas, GCP quotas
spl:

description: UC-4.4.17 — Cloud Quota and Service Limit Utilization: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:service_quotas` for configured audit predicates and returns actor, resource, and region context for capacity review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), detecting 'Cloud Quota and Service Limit Utilization' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.4.17 drives high-priority capacity alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Poll Service Quotas (or equivalent) for key limits (EC2, EBS, VPC, Lambda concurrency). Ingest current usage and quota value. Alert when utilization exceeds 80%. Dashboard all quotas with trend.
visualization: Table (quota, usage %, limit), Gauge per critical quota, Bar chart (top near-limit quotas).
knownFalsePositives: Planned load tests, new regions, and one-off batch jobs can legitimately run near limits. We treat a breach as normal when it is tied to a change ticket and a known window, and we reset after the window ends.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws`, Service Quotas API, Azure quotas, GCP quotas with the modular input for `aws:service_quotas`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Poll Service Quotas (or equivalent) for key limits (EC2, EBS, VPC, Lambda concurrency). Ingest current usage and quota value. Alert when utilization exceeds 80%. Dashboard all quotas with trend.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:service_quotas" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:service_quotas"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.17_cloud_quota_and_service_17"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:service_quotas` in `index=aws` to detect cloud quota and service limit utilization. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_17_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (quota, usage %, limit), Gauge per critical quota, Bar chart (top near-limit quotas)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws`, Service Quotas API, Azure quotas, GCP quotas and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud quota and service limit utilization so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
